questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Identify which subatomic particle defines an element's identity
questions.stem: In a software team ticket, a junior dev asks which particle determines the element's identity.

options.text: The proton, because its count is the atomic number.
The electron, because its count fixes the element's name.
options.misconception: confuses charge balance with elemental identity

options.text: The neutron, because it sets the mass number and periodic position.
options.misconception: confuses mass number with atomic identity

options.text: The photon, because light defines matter's kind.
options.misconception: treats energy quanta as material particles

questions.explanation: The element is defined by proton count; neutrons vary in isotopes and electrons vary in ions. Changing protons changes the element itself.

questions.learningObjective: Count valence electrons for group 2
questions.stem: A ticket: magnesium is in group 2; report its valence electron count.
questions.explanation: Main-group valence electrons match the group's ones digit, so group 2 gives 2. Magnesium has two valence electrons.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Identify element from configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p3
questions.stem: A ticket shows configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p3; name the element.

options.text: Chlorine, with 17 electrons.
Sulfur, with 16 electrons.
Silicon, with 14 electrons.
Phosphorus, with 15 electrons.

questions.explanation: Summing superscripts gives 15 electrons, matching phosphorus. The 3p3 pattern is phosphorus's valence.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Determine charge of an ion with 16 protons and 18 electrons
questions.stem: A ticket lists 16 protons and 18 electrons; compute the ion charge.
questions.explanation: Charge is protons minus electrons, so 16 minus 18 equals -2. The species is an anion.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Find neutrons for zinc-65
questions.stem: A ticket gives mass number 65 and atomic number 30; find the neutron count.
questions.explanation: Neutrons equal mass number minus atomic number, so 65 minus 30 equals 35. This is zinc-65.
questions.hint: Subtract atomic number from mass number.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Solve for isotope abundance with masses 39 and 41
questions.stem: A ticket: isotope masses 39 and 41 with average 39.1; find abundance of mass-41 isotope.
questions.explanation: Let x be fraction of mass-41: 39(1-x)+41x=39.1 gives x=0.05. The mass-41 isotope is 5 percent abundant.
